QF.id: Registration, Code of Conduct and General Obligations_49

question.text: Under Rule 9 of the Code of Conduct, on what grounds is a merchant banker PERMITTED to discriminate among its clients?

answer.text: Based on the size of the client's portfolio
Based on the client's geographic location
Discrimination is never permitted under any circumstances

explanation.text: The Logic: The Code of Conduct states that a merchant banker shall not discriminate amongst its clients save and except on ethical and commercial considerations. This carve-out is the only basis on which differential treatment of clients is permitted. The Trap: "Discrimination is never permitted" sounds like the strictest and therefore safest answer, but the rule explicitly allows the ethical/commercial considerations exception. Portfolio size and geographic location are not recognized bases under this provision. Note: The carve-out is narrow — it covers ethical and commercial considerations only, and does not extend to arbitrary client preferences.
